title: McKinney man indicted in Jefferson County after I-10 stop finds 400g codeine - NewsBreak
text:
By Megan Zapalac ,
12 hours ago More than half of U.S. female lawyers surveyed reported being sexually harassed in the workplace. (Dreamstime/TNS) (Dreamstime, HO) A McKinney man has been indicted after a traffic stop in Jefferson County revealed over 400 grams of Codeine and a handgun.
The 28-year-old man was indicted by a Jefferson County grand jury on Sept. 17 for possession of a controlled substance over 400 grams.
Just before 9:25 a.m. on Feb. 17, a Jefferson County Sheriff's Detective was patrolling when they pulled over an SUV on Interstate 10 westbound that was going 70 mph in a 55 mph construction zone and having an expired license plate, according to a police report from the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office.
After making contact with the suspect and the 32-year-old driver, the officer smelled marijuana coming from the vehicle, the sheriff's office said.
Both men gave conflicting stories about where they were coming from, where they stayed, how long they were there and where they were going, according to the report.

A routine check of both men showed that the driver had an outstanding felony drug warrant out of Travis County.
A probable cause search led the detective to find a backpack on the right rear passenger seat with a Glock 43 handgun, 9x19 and over 400 grams of Codeine in several bottles, the Sheriff's Office said. Both men denied knowledge of the bag and what was inside of it.
Before being arrested, the 28-year-old gave the detective a bag of marijuana that he had on his person, the report stated.
Both men were arrested for possession of a controlled substance over 400 grams and unlawful carrying of a weapon by a felon.
